title: Fresh Orange Peel Sauce for Orange Chicken
description: Fresh orange juice makes the body of this sauce, while grated zest added at the end supplies the orange-oil aroma.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain homemade or unsalted carton broth at about 35 mg sodium per cup, with household-approved ingredients.

ingredients.name: coconut aminos
ingredients.note: Use Coconut Secret Original at 90 mg sodium per teaspoon. Low-sodium batch: use 1 tsp total.

ingredients.name: fresh ginger juice
ingredients.note: Finely grate peeled ginger and squeeze out the juice.

steps.title: Reduce the orange
steps.text: Simmer {oj} and {ch} in the HexClad for 5–6 minutes until the liquid smells distinctly of orange.

steps.title: Season the reduction
steps.text: Stir in {a}, {ho}, {gi} and {rv}. Simmer for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Release the orange oils
steps.text: Rub {oz} between your fingertips over the pan and stir it in just before thickening.

steps.title: Mix the slurry
steps.text: Stir {sl} into {cw} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Whisk the slurry into the gently simmering base. Cook for 60–90 seconds, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Check the yield
steps.text: Measure the sauce in a heatproof cup. Aim for 1 cup. If short, loosen with a little hot sodium-free water. If over, return it to the pan and simmer briefly to the mark.

steps.title: Serve the sauce
steps.text: Spoon over tender cutlets or shrimp just before serving so the fresh peel stays fragrant.

notes: Yield: 1 cup, or four 1/4-cup portions. Low-sodium option for the full batch: Use 1 tsp coconut aminos in place of 4 tsp. Use the same final 1-cup yield and 1/4-cup serving. Make ahead: Make the sauce the day before and portion it before chilling. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze flat in 1/4-cup portions for up to 2 months. Whisk again after thawing to restore the texture. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion in a small pan, stirring to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Loosen with a splash of water if it tightens. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator, then use the fridge reheat method. Option A uses the listed seasonings. For a gentler Option B, replace half the juice with water, skip the vinegar and halve the zest. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/4 of recipe): 49 kcal, 0.5 g protein, 11.9 g total carbohydrate, 0.1 g fat, 0.2 g fiber, 93 mg sodium. Low-sodium version per 1/4 cup: 45 kcal, 0.5 g protein, 10.9 g total carbohydrate, 0.1 g fat, 0.2 g fiber, 26 mg sodium. Figures cover the sauce alone. Sodium varies with brands.

steps.text: Start the enamel Dutch oven over medium-low heat for 2–3 minutes; use the lid for covered steps. Reduce heat once liquids simmer and stir across the heavy base.
